items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Both of us recorded with Jackie McLean and Horace Silver, and both worked in the Horace Silver band

ctx.x: Okay. “Operated on a minimal finances, maximal passion, a pivotal platform for the independent jazz movement that emerged from Civil Rights in the 1970s.

Okay. Okay. It didn’t emerge from the Civil Rights Movement because my idea to do an independent endeavor like this stemmed from let’s say two events. First of all, when I was coming up and you really got into this, you either got your own leader date at Blue Note or one of the other independents that was going on at the time. That didn’t happen to me nor did it happen for Woody Shaw, because both of us were coming up at the same time. It should have, you know, because of who we recorded with on Blue Note. Both…

completely different in terms of the historical thing of my career had that happened. So by 1968, ’69, I was already, I already had this what was going to become Strata-East records. I was going to do it, it was just a matter of time. And because my dear Stanley Cowell and I were so close you know, every day, and working with Max Roach and watching what he did it was inevitable at that particular time, in 1970, that we were going to go in the studio and make a recording which would be the first record to launch…
